messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: elevated 5xx spike across hosted API (edge -> gateway). Initial alert at 1758022468. Please acknowledge with `ack`.

maya: ack — I'm on it. Seeing spikes in gateway 502/504 and a small fanout of 429s upstream.

raj: I can join, looking at env metrics. Any customer-visible degradations reported?

support-bot: Several support tickets created: 3 customers reporting timeouts, one reporting repeated 429s. Ticket IDs #6741, #6745, #6747.

cory: I can confirm error-rate jump around 1758022400. P50 latency looks normal but P99 and tails are saturating. Errors are mostly gateway timeout & 502.

lina: Running `kubectl get pods -n api` shows a couple of edge-proxy pods in CrashLoopBackOff, restart loop around 1758022435. Logs show `http: upstream read timeout` and `429 response from rate-limiter`.

ethan: Interesting — rate-limiter reported quota exhaustion on the global bucket for a short window. We had a policy change rolled out ~1758022000 that tightened token refill for burst smoothing.

maya: Can you paste the policy diff?

ethan: Here: ```diff
--- old
+ global_rate_limit: 1000rps
- global_rate_limit: 3000rps
 token_bucket:
   refill: 1000
   capacity: 2000
+ sticky_flow: true
```

priya: That sticky_flow flag was experimental (rollout flag 0.23). If sticky buckets stayed sticky to particular gateways, some gateways might have drained while others overflowed.

raj: I'm seeing a cascade: gateway A hit 429s -> clients retried -> increased load on gateway B -> B exhausted KV cache for rate limits -> 502s.

maya: Mitigation proposal: rollback the ratepolicy change (disable sticky_flow and restore previous refill) and temporarily scale up rate-limiter replicas + increase token bucket capacity. Can someone run rollback?

cory: Rolling back the feature flag now via the control plane: `featurectl disable sticky_flow --env=prod`. Pushing in 2m.

incident-bot: action: feature flag disable requested by cory at 1758022510.

lina: While rollback is in flight, let's add a routing fallback: route 10% of traffic to Dedicated fallback model (lower QPS, less batching) to relieve hosted clusters. I can add a temporary route rule.

priya: Agree. Also suggest enabling short-circuit 429->503 fallback at the gateway so we present a stable error rather than tight retry storms.

ethan: Increasing rate-limiter replica count from 3 -> 8 now. Command: `kubectl scale deployment rate-limiter -n infra --replicas=8`. Doing it.

maya: Scaling performed. Watching token refill counters — they are trending up.

support-bot: Noted. Customer-facing update: "We're investigating increased error rates across the API and have implemented mitigations. We'll update in 15 minutes." I'll post to all affected ticket threads.

raj: Post-rollback metrics: 1758022580 — 429s dropped by ~70%, 502s decreased but still above baseline. Tail latency improving.

cory: Feature flag rollback confirmed: `featurectl status sticky_flow` -> disabled at 1758022560.

lina: Gateway pod restarts ceased after rollback and scaling. No more CrashLoopBackOffs.

priya: I deployed the temporary routing rule to send 10% to Dedicated fallback at 1758022605. That reduced burst pressure on the global token bucket.

ethan: Running a quick health check across regions — EU region shows similar but smaller blip. Likely propagation delay during the policy rollout. We should validate our rollout guard to prevent global sticky policies without canary.

maya: Actions so far: 1) rollback sticky_flow flag 2) scale rate-limiter -> 8 replicas 3) temporary routing shift 10% -> Dedicated fallback 4) short-circuit 429->503 at gateway 5) customer comms.

raj: Agreed next steps: a) revert the ratepolicy change entirely from the config repo and add a canary rollout (10% traffic for 30m) b) add alert for token-bucket skew between nodes c) postmortem owner.

cory: I'll open the revert PR and restrict rollout to canary only. PR #1298 opened.

incident-bot: Note: On-call handoff scheduled in 30m to lina.

lina: I'll take on-call for the next shift. I'll monitor error-rate and customer tickets. If errors remain >2% for 15m we escalate to SRE pager.

support-bot: Updated customers with ETA and mitigation steps. Some asked for SLA credit explanation — routed to CS lead.

priya: For the postmortem: we should capture the rollout path, why sticky_flow was enabled globally, missing canary, and the retry fanout amplification. I'll volunteer to be PM for the postmortem.

maya: Great. Paging summary for the postmortem: root cause = aggressive ratepolicy sticky token buckets rolled globally; contributing = lack of canary and insufficient node-level token skew alerts; mitigation = disable flag, scaled replicas, routing fallback, gateway short-circuit, revert PR.

ethan: Logging note: we should add more granular metrics on per-bucket utilization and per-gateway backlog to catch this earlier. I'll file infra ticket.

cory: System health now stable. 5xx returned to baseline by 1758022760. Closing pager but keep this thread live for the postmortem artifacts.

incident-bot: Pager closed at 1758022780 by cory.

maya: Thanks team. I'll draft customer-facing root cause and connect with CS.

priya: Postmortem owner: priya. Target publish: 72 hours.

support-bot: Closing tickets with summary and linking postmortem when available.

lina: Leaving a note in runbook: do not enable sticky_flow globally without canary and add a checklist for ratepolicy rollouts.

maya: End of thread — keeping logs & metrics snapshot attached to PM.
